newsitem.title: USA: More rain for Ohio River Valley, wheat areas warm.
newsitem.headline: More rain for Ohio River Valley, wheat areas warm.

text.p: Rain was forecast for the Ohio River Valley late Monday and Tuesday and more rain was expected there late this week, meterologists said.
"It (the area) appears to be in a wet pattern that will continue," said Joel Burgio, meteorologist with Weather Services Corp.

Hard winter wheat areas from Kansas to Texas had sub-freezing weather early Saturday, but temperatures shot up to the 70's degrees Fahrenheit by Sunday. The highs should edge down Monday and Tuesday only to return to the 70s Thursday and Friday.
Burgio doubts this week's rain in the Ohio River Valley will spark renewed flooding, but it should keep river levels high.
"To get back to where we were we would need a big two- to three-inch rain," he said.
However, he said current weather patterns suggest a parade of storms will march through that area the next several weeks.
Fred Gesser, Weather Express Inc meteorologist, forecast 0.50 to two inches of rain, locally heavier, for much of the Ohio River Valley late Monday and Tuesday.
He said this is will be from the same storm system that produced about 4.5 inches of rain this past weekend near Victoria, Texas, about 100 miles southwest of Houston.

The hard red winter wheat areas in western Kansas went from a frigid 10 to 15 degrees Saturday to near 80s Sunday. Some cooling was likely Monday and Tuesday, but temperatures should return to the 70s Wednesday and Thursday, meteorogolists said.
Beneficial precipitation, probably rain, was expected in the Kansas wheat areas late this week, said Gesser.
More snow fell in the Dakotas and Montana with two to four inches of accumulation by Tuesday, and another two to four inches likely Friday and Saturday, said Gesser
Minor flooding could occur in western Washington from rain expect there, said WSC's Burgio. he said 0.5 to an inch was forecast Monday and another 0.5 to two inches on Tuesday.
